appraisal_events.evidence: Vous savez pourquoi on ne peut pas montrer les preuves de la trahison de Dreyfus. Il paraît que c'est parce qu'il est l'amant de la femme du ministre de la Guerre, cela se dit sous le manteau.
appraisal_events.explanation: An unnamed salon voice accuses Dreyfus of treason and, in the same breath, offers a frivolous adulterous explanation for the withheld evidence; the absurdity of the reasoning frames the accusation as unreliable salon gossip rather than an endorsed judgment.

status_effects.explanation: He is discussed only as the object of an unverified, frivolous treason/adultery rumor circulating among the salon guests, a mild local discredit tempered by the narrator's evident irony toward the gossipers.

ambiguities: The speaker of the line about Dreyfus's alleged treason and affair is not clearly attributed (it falls between the duke's remark to Argencourt and Argencourt's reply), so the exact source of the gossip is uncertain; it is treated here as an unnamed collective social voice.
le narrateur is present only as observing consciousness in this salon scene and is not staged as a social participant, so he was not scored.
